maml:description.maml:para: Converts a version string to a four-component .NET Version.

The ConvertTo-DotNetVersionClass function converts a version string to a four-component .NET Version. Periods, underscores, plus signs, and hyphens separate components. Numeric components must use ASCII digits. Text components are mapped to stable SHA-256-derived integers; this allows conversion but does not preserve semantic version ordering, so the resulting .NET Version should not be used to compare prerelease or other text-labeled versions.

Components after the third are summed into the fourth component, which saturates at Int32.MaxValue. Versions with fewer than four components are padded with zeros. Invalid or out-of-range numeric components result in an error.
A version string to convert to a standard .NET compliant version class.

maml:description.maml:para: Removes old application installer versions from an Evergreen library while keeping the newest versions in each application manifest.
`Remove-EvergreenLibraryAppVersion` prunes historical versions from an Evergreen library application manifest.

The cmdlet validates that `-Path` points to an Evergreen library by checking for `EvergreenLibrary.json`. For each target application, it reads the app manifest (`<ApplicationName>.json`), sorts versions from newest to oldest, keeps the number of entries defined by `-Keep`, removes older installer files from disk, and writes the retained versions back to the app manifest.
By default, all applications in the library are processed and the latest 3 versions are retained.

The keep limit counts individual manifest entries in both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. The retained manifest remains a JSON array, even when `-Keep 1` is used. Installer paths can be absolute, relative to the application directory, or arrays of paths recorded by older module versions. Only installer files recorded in pruned entries are removed, and files also referenced by retained entries are preserved. Paths outside the application directory and paths traversing reparse points are skipped. Empty version directories are not removed.
Files left behind by an earlier prune cannot be removed by rerunning this cmdlet if their entries are no longer in the manifest. This cmdlet does not scan for unrecorded installer files.

Use `-Verbose` to troubleshoot library validation, application selection, manifest reads, version sorting, retained and pruned entries, skipped installer files, and manifest updates. Messages distinguish planned pruning from files actually removed and report actions skipped by `-WhatIf` or declined confirmation. Verbose messages do not change the returned objects.

maml:description.maml:para: Invokes the update and download of application installers in an Evergreen library. `Start-EvergreenLibraryUpdate` reads the library manifest (`EvergreenLibrary.json`) which defines the applications in the library and uses `Get-EvergreenApp` and `Save-EvergreenApp` to download the latest installers to the library.

An Evergreen library can be used to maintain multiple versions of application installers, rather than always using the latest installer. An Evergreen library allows you to install the version of an application required for a specific environment including rolling back to a previous version of an application. An Evergreen library also enables you to build an image build without requiring internet access, by downloading the application installers to the library and then using those installers during the image build process.

`Start-EvergreenLibraryUpdate` invokes the update and download of application installers in an Evergreen library. `Start-EvergreenLibraryUpdate` reads the library manifest (`EvergreenLibrary.json`) which defines the applications in the library and uses `Get-EvergreenApp` and `Save-EvergreenApp` to download the latest installers to the library.
Specifies the path to the Evergreen library. The path must include EvergreenLibrary.json, in the expected structure, which defines the applications to be stored in the library.

maml:description.maml:para: Validates target URIs passed to this function from `Get-EvergreenApp`.

Evergreen includes the function `Test-EvergreenApp` that validates application installer URLs returned from `Get-EvergreenApp`. It first sends a HEAD request and retries failed requests with a ranged GET. The output includes the result, HTTP status code when available, and URI.

`Test-EvergreenApp` accepts application objects from `Get-EvergreenApp` and requires a non-empty URI property. Invalid objects produce a warning and a false result; processing continues for subsequent objects.

maml:description.maml:para: Downloads and synchronizes the Evergreen Apps functions and Manifests from the eucpilots/evergreen-apps GitHub repository.

Enables separation of the core Evergreen module from app-specific code and manifests. Downloads the latest versions of /Apps and /Manifests from a specified GitHub repository to a user-writable location (no admin required). By default, the local cache is downloaded to %LocalAppData%\Evergreen on Windows, and ~/.evergreen on macOS and Linux.
